Unlike sequence labeling methods that label each input word with a predefined category, we regard DIE as a translation task that translates source OCR results to a structured format (like key-value pairs in this paper).

Unlike sequence labeling methods that label each input word with a predefined category, we regard DIE as a translation task that translates source OCR results to a structured format (like key-value pairs in this paper). We use UniLM as the basic model structure, which is a transformer-based pre-trained network that can handle both natural language understanding (NLU) and natural language generation (NLG) tasks simultaneously. Conditioned on a sequence of source words, GMN generates one word at each time step to compose a series of key-value pairs in them.
outputs: Structured key-value pairs extracted from document images
